messages:
alex: Heads-up — we need to roll a GPU watchdog firmware sweep across the euc2 GPU pool this Wednesday 03:00–06:00 UTC. This will cause one-by-one node reboots; aim is <30s hard-reboot per node but pods will be evicted briefly. I’ll exclude Dedicated pools with active contracts. More below.

sara: Which exact node groups? any Dedicated/Reserved customers affected?

alex: Affected groups: gpool-euc2-a, gpool-euc2-b, gpool-euc2-backfill. Dedicated pools (ded-gpool-euc2-*) are excluded. The vendor flagged nv-watchdog microcode for these specific machines.

jordan: Plan for cordon+drain? backfill from other regions or local on-demand? Warmup kv/prefix caches?

alex: Yes — we’ll cordon then drain with graceful eviction, then reboot. Backfill strategy: local on-demand warm backfill first, fall back to us-west spill if capacity dips >8%. We'll do a 2-node canary then ramp. Recommended drain command:

```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# check pods: kubectl get pods -o wide -n infra-workloads
```

Also warm up prefix cache after each pair of reboots to avoid cold-start latency spikes (we have a script in infra/tools/warmup-prefix.sh).

ops-bot: :calendar: Maintenance scheduled — GPU Watchdog Firmware Sweep — Wed 03:00–06:00 UTC — https://calendar.redwood/meet/maintenance/1794567890

maya: Quick flag on cost: if we backfill with on-demand instances to maintain 99p latency, expect ~ $1.2k/hr across the window given current instance mix. Suggest we allow a short p95 blip instead of full on-demand backfill to save $~3k for the window.

vincent: Routing note — if we spill to us-west we’ll incur cross-region egress charges and higher latency for some tenants. Can we prefer intra-region fallback (eu-central) and degrade non-critical batch jobs first?

alex: Good call — prefer eu-central candidates. We’ll lower batch window size and pause non-critical training jobs for the 3-hour window. Canary sequence: drain 2 nodes -> wait 10m -> verify p95 & error-rate -> proceed by 4-node cohorts.

jordan: Oncall / escalation? If a node fails to come back or NV resets repeatedly we need hw-pager and cloud ops engaged. Runbook here: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/gpu-firmware-failures

alex: Oncall is @infra-oncall (pager) + @hw-pager. If >5% pool capacity lost we post to #incidents and trigger rollback plan. Rollback is to suspend firmware apply and reprovision from snapshot. Escalation timeline in runbook: reboot retry x3 then escalate.

maya: Can we pre-warm a small pool (5 nodes) 30m before to absorb initial traffic? small cost but reduces error surface.

alex: Yes — we’ll pre-warm 5 nodes and keep them ready for 45m. That’s the canary pool.

vincent: One more thing: ensure routing policy honors reserved capacity tags so Dedicated customers never move.

alex: Affirmed — reserved tags will be respected by the scheduler; Dedicated pools are off-limits. I’ll add a quick checklist for the ops runbook and post it before the window.

sara: Thanks — please include a short customer comms note we can hand to Support + CSMs if they get pinged.

alex: Will do. Draft will go to #customer-success for approval 24h before.

jordan: I’ll be online for the canary and first cohort.

alex: Great — I'll post live updates here during the window. If anyone sees p95 spike >20% or error-rate up, ping me directly. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Reminder scheduled 1h before window starts.
